subject.title: fix(exec): stop isolated state dirs from moving live approvals

question: Should OpenClaw permanently retire cross-state approval relocation, or retain an explicit operator-confirmed migration path for users moving a pre-2026.6.6 primary state directory?
rationale: The repository cannot distinguish an isolated test or secondary instance from an intentional primary-state relocation solely from `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; choosing whether and how restrictive approval policy crosses that boundary is a security and upgrade-contract decision.

options.title: Retain explicit import
options.body: Keep automatic and non-interactive cross-state imports disabled, but provide an operator-confirmed Doctor migration for a specifically identified source state directory.

options.title: Retire relocation migration
options.body: Accept the compatibility break, add an unavoidable Doctor warning and release guidance, and prove that users cannot silently enter a more permissive execution policy.

options.title: Defer to SQLite cutover
options.body: Pause this broad deletion until the coordinated same-state JSON-to-SQLite migration can provide one canonical approval transition.

recommendation.title: Retain explicit import
recommendation.body: Keep automatic and non-interactive cross-state imports disabled, but provide an operator-confirmed Doctor migration for a specifically identified source state directory.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored both the merged capability-based isolation mitigation and this broader trust-scope change.
